answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each agent to one auditable reputation identity that costs real work to build: like a falcon returning to a single beacon, an agent must accumulate verified task history before it can transact at full value. A pigment-like fingerprint, a hash of its prior attestations and completed contracts, makes cloning expensive, because a fresh copy starts with zero history and cannot borrow another agent's record, so attackers must spend weeks earning trust per identity or stay cheap and powerless.
